result:
Done. `final.py` is a LIRS cache (Low Inter-reference Recency Set) with a 5% HIR share. Search score 0.566, 9 of 24 scorer calls used.

| Candidate | Harness train | Harness held-out | Official search score |
|---|---|---|---|
| Baseline LRU | 0.423 | 0.435 | 0.365 |
| First champion: ARC | 0.444 | 0.457 | 0.407 |
| Final pick: LIRS, 5% HIR | 0.444 | 0.463 | 0.566 |

**Why it wins.** LRU and ARC thrash on loops longer than the cache. LIRS ranks keys by reuse distance instead of recency, so a loop's members become the protected LIR set and the small HIR queue absorbs scans and one-off keys. On the scorer the loop traces went from 0.16 and 0.30 under ARC to 0.80 and 0.64, while recency only dipped from 0.85 to 0.80. The three remaining trace kinds sat at the same level for every family tried, so they look near their ceiling.

**Families tried in step 3.** ARC (champion, 0.407 official), TinyLFU (fixed window killed the recency trace), 2Q, LFU with aging, and S3-FIFO all landed below ARC on the harness. LIRS was the only family to move loops, so the rounds then explored it: HIR share from 1% to 40%, stack depth from 2× to 16× capacity, a ghost-driven adaptive HIR, a hill-climbing HIR, a FIFO HIR queue, and a gentler stack trim. Only the HIR share mattered; 5% with a 3× stack was best on the scorer.

**Budget.** Default mode of about 15 minutes, started 23:17 and used about 9 minutes. The clock reading mid-run misled me once into announcing the budget spent early, so I corrected course and kept searching. The full log is in `CANDIDATES.log` beside the candidates. Time per trace is well inside the limit at roughly 0.14 seconds per 300k requests.

**Caveats.** Selection used the official search split, so the 0.566 is optimistic. My harness is only loosely calibrated, with the baseline reading 0.42 there versus 0.365 officially, and its recency trace penalizes LIRS more than the scorer's does. The hidden-split result could land somewhere between the hill-climb variant and the fixed pick, but every LIRS point scored 0.52 to 0.57, well above ARC.
